_about: The Data desk's own fields for each outside source (datadesk/registry.py), over reference/data_sources.json and static/research/permit_sources.json, which stay as they are. Keyed by source id: a catalogue source's id is its name in lower case with hyphens; a permit dataset's is permit:<its id>. Only what was decided by hand is here; every other field is worked out from the lists, and the loaded source names those in derived. route: server | pc | import | git; access: open | key | sign-in | form | paid; owner: Cody, or Josh for anything paid or contractual.

wigle.why: WiGLE refuses the server's cloud address (11/7); its personal key is for its holder's own machine, so Cody's PC fetches (ops/crowd_pull.py) and sends the points to the server. Never a route round a terms refusal.

repeaterbook.note: Its terms bar multi-source tools and commercial use without paid access; a PC pull doesn't change the terms.
repeaterbook.person_task: Ask RepeaterBook for permission or paid access for DAStastic's use, or find a permitted source for the same repeaters.

fcc-uls-daily-change-files.note: Terms read 2026-11-08 by Cody in his own browser (www.fcc.gov answers automated clients 403, so DAStastic doesn't fetch the page): the page lists the daily and weekly files with no terms, copyright notice or use restriction; its footer points to the FCC's general Website Policies & Notices. US government data (17 U.S.C. 105). data.fcc.gov serves the files themselves to DAStastic's own client (fetchkit, conditional requests).

fcc-911-psap-registry.note: fcc.gov refuses automated clients, so a person downloads the registry's CSV from that page (Cody did 11/8: masterpsapregistryv2.301, as of 2026-10-30) and tools/psap_registry.py reads it into reference/psap_registry.json. The FCC posts a new one every six weeks or so. US government data.

fcc-signal-booster-registrations-class-b.note: Terms read 2026-11-08 on the item page (and its metadata, https://www.arcgis.com/sharing/rest/content/items/636f8803adbb431aa9324efbee3489e2?f=json): a public ArcGIS layer from the FCC's own ArcGIS organisation (YnOQrIGdN9JGtBh4), the one behind the FCC's app Signal Booster Registration Information (https://experience.arcgis.com/experience/558fa854f397424fa188dff89750d4c3); access public, no licence or use restriction on the item. US government data (17 U.S.C. 105). It answers DAStastic's own client (fetchkit) with an ETag and Last-Modified, and takes resultRecordCount (pages of 2,000). People's details (Cody 11/8, "Keep everything"): the registrants' named contacts (company_attention, every contact_* field, company_email, company_phone, company_phone_1, signature, signature_title, and the company's street address and ZIP) go in their own table, booster_contact, kept on the server and Cody's PC only (the personal build) and read only by an admin. Never in field packs, the web version or GitHub Pages, the repo's reference/ data, the install kit or logs. The switch that blocks prospect emails is unchanged. Everything else (registration number, position, building address, location description, call signs, frequencies, company name, city and state, dates) is business data and shows anywhere the app shows data.
